records.text: Victor Marx announced his Colorado gubernatorial run at a Charlie Kirk memorial event in Denver on September 14.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: He is currently, you should know, running for governor of Colorado, and he chose to make, to announce his intention to run for governor of Colorado at a Charlie Kirk memorial event in Denver on September 14th, just a couple of days after Charlie (Charlie Kirk) was assassinated. He said... ... that he felt in that moment, given the weight of the assassination, that God was calling him to run.

verification.notes: Contemporaneous reporting confirms Marx spoke at the September 14 Charlie Kirk memorial and dropped explicit hints that he planned to seek the governorship. It also dates his formal campaign announcement to October 1, so calling the memorial itself the announcement overstates what occurred there.

sources.title: Colorado Politics: Victor Marx joins gubernatorial primary
sources.relevance: Reports the October 1 formal launch and says the September 14 memorial contained explicit hints.

records.text: Candace Owens said Victor Marx was running for governor of Colorado and, according to him, was inspired by Charlie Kirk's death.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Anyway, now we know Victor is running for governor of Colorado, inspired by, according to him, Charlie's untimely death.

verification.notes: Colorado campaign records and the Marx campaign site confirm that he is a candidate for governor. Launch materials prominently invoked Charlie Kirk and used a Charlie Wave initiative, but the reviewed primary campaign pages did not clearly state that the death of Kirk itself caused Marx to run. The candidacy is confirmed; the stated motivation is only partly supported.

sources.title: Victor Marx Launches Campaign for Governor
sources.relevance: Campaign launch page links the effort to a Charlie Wave but does not clearly say the death of Kirk caused the candidacy.

verification.notes: In temporal context on May 20, 2026, Marx was leading a May 11 campaign-aligned Republican-primary poll at 59 percent and later narrowly won the GOP primary. The broader wording that he was winning the governor race overstates what that partisan primary poll established and did not show he was leading the statewide general election.
